name: 20 Bridges (Manhattan Island)
why: The circumnavigation of Manhattan is a leg of the Triple Crown of marathon swimming, run by NYC Swim's successor NY Open Water with tide-timed starts.
heads_up: Tide windows, commercial traffic, water-quality closures

name: Acadia National Park
why: Otter Cliffs is America's iconic sea-cliff crag, and the Precipice, Beehive and Cadillac trails are its most-hiked coastal routes.
heads_up: Peregrine closures on Precipice in spring; summer crowds

name: Acapulco
why: Club de Yates de Acapulco hosted the 1968 Olympic sailing regatta and remains Mexico's historic Pacific regatta bay.
heads_up: Check current security advisories; humid heat

name: Adirondack High Peaks
why: The 46 High Peaks from Adirondak Loj and the Ausable Club are the Northeast's most storied peak-bagging circuit.
heads_up: Parking permits at AMR; mud season closures in spring

name: Ajusco / Desierto de los Leones
why: Mexico City's home mountains with long-established singletrack above 3,000 m that hosts the capital's race scene.
heads_up: High altitude; small access fee and rainy afternoons Jun-Sep

name: Akumal Bay turtles
why: The Riviera Maya's turtle-snorkelling bay, with a government-run guide system and one of the oldest dive centres on the coast.
heads_up: Guided access and life-jacket rules; crowding

name: Alcatraz / Aquatic Park
why: The most famous open-water swim in North America, with the Dolphin Club and South End Rowing Club swimming Aquatic Park daily since the 1870s and dozens of organised Alcatraz crossings a year.
heads_up: 50-60F water, shipping traffic, strong tidal currents; escorted crossings only

name: Alger Underwater Preserve
why: Michigan's first underwater preserve, with intact shallow wrecks like the Bermuda and sea caves below Pictured Rocks, serviced by a dedicated shipwreck-tour operator.
heads_up: Very cold water, weather cancellations; no artifact removal

name: Algonquin Park (Canoe Lake)
why: Thirty-four access points and 2,000 km of routes; Canoe Lake is the classic starting point with outfitters at the gate.
heads_up: Backcountry reservations; portages and black bears

name: Alta
why: 500-plus inches of Little Cottonwood powder, skier-only tradition since 1938 and the Wasatch's legendary steeps.
heads_up: Snowboards not allowed; canyon road closes for avalanche control

name: Alyeska
why: Alaska's only major resort: 650 inches of maritime snow, 2,500 ft of vertical from sea level and heli operations out the door.
heads_up: Short daylight in Dec-Jan; coastal storms

name: Anchorage (Kincaid / Hillside)
why: Singletrack Advocates-built networks at Kincaid Park and Hillside are Alaska's established riding, with midnight-sun summer seasons.
heads_up: Moose and bear encounters; short season

name: Angel Fire Bike Park
why: The Rockies' largest bike park by trail mileage, 2,000 ft of lift-served vertical and host of national downhill and enduro events.
heads_up: Altitude over 8,600 ft at base

name: Annapolis
why: America's Sailing Capital: the US Naval Academy fleet, the Annapolis Sailboat Show, Wednesday night racing and the Chesapeake's largest racing scene.
heads_up: Hot, light summer wind; crowded city dock

name: Apostle Islands
why: The mainland sea caves off Meyers Beach and 21 islands make this the Great Lakes' signature sea-kayak destination with guided tours from Bayfield.
heads_up: Cold water and sudden squalls; deaths at the caves; no sit-on-tops

name: Appalachian Trail (Springer Mountain)
why: Amicalola Falls and Springer Mountain are the start of the 2,190-mile AT, where thousands of thru-hikers set off every spring.
heads_up: Register with the ATC; March crowds at shelters

name: Arapahoe Basin
why: The Legend: 13,050 ft summit, Pallavicini steeps, the Beach tailgate scene and a season that regularly runs into June.
heads_up: Extreme altitude and wind-exposed upper mountain

name: Arches National Park
why: Delicate Arch and the Devils Garden loop are Moab's bucket-list day hikes.
heads_up: Timed-entry reservations; no shade, summer heat

name: Arkansas River (Browns Canyon, Numbers, Royal Gorge)
why: The most commercially rafted river in the US, with Browns Canyon National Monument, The Numbers and Royal Gorge all within an hour of Buena Vista and Salida.
heads_up: Altitude (8,000 ft) and cold snowmelt in June

name: Ascension Bay (Punta Allen)
why: The best permit flats on earth inside the Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve, with the Caribbean's deepest grand-slam lodge network.
heads_up: Rough road to Punta Allen; wind and cold fronts in winter; lodges book far ahead

name: Ashland
why: Ashland Watershed trails with 4,000 ft shuttle descents from Mt Ashland and a long-running local shuttle service.
heads_up: Summer wildfire smoke; shuttle fees

name: Aspen (Aspen Mountain)
why: Gondola-accessed 11,000 ft launch flown by Aspen Paragliding for decades, with a town-adjacent LZ and big mountain XC.
heads_up: High altitude, strong thermals and afternoon storms; intermediate-plus with site intro

name: Aspen Snowmass
why: Four mountains on one ticket, host of the X Games, with Highland Bowl among the most celebrated inbounds hikes in the country, and an IMBA Gold-level Ride Center with Snowmass Bike Park and 300+ miles of valley singletrack.
heads_up: Expensive; Highland Bowl requires a 45-minute bootpack

name: Au Sable River (Grayling)
why: The birthplace of Trout Unlimited and the Au Sable riverboat, famous for the Hex hatch and the 'Holy Waters' flies-only stretch.
heads_up: Night fishing for Hex; flies-only catch-and-release on the Holy Waters

name: Bahía Concepción
why: Calm, warm water and island hopping from Playa Santispac, a NOLS sea-kayak course venue and winter snowbird paddling base.
heads_up: Morning north wind; summer heat above 40°C

name: Bahía de los Ángeles
why: Dozens of islands and summer whale sharks in a remote Sea of Cortez bay, run for decades by expedition outfitters.
heads_up: Remote; strong afternoon winds; limited services

name: Banco Chinchorro
why: The largest coral atoll in the Northern Hemisphere, with pristine reef, wrecks and licensed American-crocodile snorkels run by permit-holding operators from Xcalak and Mahahual.
heads_up: Permit-limited, weather-dependent crossing; remote

name: Banzai Pipeline
why: The most famous wave in the world and the finale of the Vans Triple Crown, breaking in front of Ehukai Beach Park.
heads_up: Deadly shallow reef; elite-only lineup in winter; packed parking

name: Barra de la Cruz
why: A community-managed world-class right point that hosted the 2006 Rip Curl Search WCT event.
heads_up: Community entry fee; sand-dependent; heat and limited lodging

name: Barton Springs Pool
why: A three-acre 68F spring-fed pool swum year-round, the most famous natural swimming venue in Texas and a lap-swimming institution.
heads_up: Closed Thursdays for cleaning; entry fee; crowded summer afternoons

name: Battenkill River
why: The storied home river of Orvis and the American Museum of Fly Fishing, with notoriously difficult wild browns.
heads_up: Very technical, spooky fish; catch-and-release regs in Vermont

name: Beaver Creek
why: Annual World Cup downhill on the Birds of Prey course and immaculate grooming make it a destination in its own right.
heads_up: Pricey; limited expert steeps compared to neighbours

name: Bell Island WWII wrecks
why: Four ore carriers torpedoed by U-boats in 1942 lie close together off Bell Island, a world-renowned cold-water wreck site served by Ocean Quest Adventures.
heads_up: Advanced only; frigid water; unexploded ordnance

name: Belmont Shore, Long Beach
why: The only LA/Orange County beach where kite lessons are permitted; flat water behind the breakwater and 100+ kites on a good day.
heads_up: Ultra crowded; no riding within 200 ft of shore in swim season

name: Bend
why: 300+ miles of COTA-maintained singletrack (Phil's, Wanoga, Mt Bachelor park) in a town built around bikes.
heads_up: Dust in late summer; upper trails snowbound until June

name: Bend / Deschutes River
why: Central Oregon's SUP hub, with Tumalo Creek Kayak & Canoe rentals at Riverbend Park and the Old Mill float.
heads_up: Class II at Colorado Avenue whitewater park; cold snowmelt water

name: Bentonville
why: Walton-funded, purpose-built trail city (Slaughter Pen, Coler, Back 40) with hundreds of miles of singletrack riding from downtown.
heads_up: Hot humid summers; weekend crowds

name: Berg Lake Trail (Mount Robson)
why: The 21 km trail past Emperor Falls to Berg Lake beneath Mount Robson is BC's flagship backpacking route.
heads_up: Rebuilt after 2021 flood; reservations required; confirm current route

name: Berkeley Marina
why: Home of the Cal Sailing Club, one of the largest volunteer sailing and windsurfing co-ops in the US, in the Bay's strongest summer wind zone (the Berkeley Circle).
heads_up: Big chop and 20+ kn afternoons

name: Berthoud Pass
why: Former ski area turned Colorado's busiest and best-known backcountry pass, with hitchable laps off the summit lot on both sides of US-40.
heads_up: Persistent slab avalanche problems; no patrol

name: Big Bear / Snow Summit
why: Southern California's lift-served bike park and long-time NORBA venue, with Skyline and Santa Ana River trails nearby.
heads_up: Weekend LA crowds; dust

name: Big Bend (South Rim)
why: The South Rim loop from Chisos Basin and the Santa Elena Canyon walk are Texas's definitive desert hikes.
heads_up: Remote; extreme summer heat; carry water

name: Big Shoulders (Ohio Street Beach)
why: The Big Shoulders 2.5K/5K has run off Ohio Street Beach since 1991, and the beach is Chicago's daily open-water training lane along the seawall.
heads_up: Lake chop and cold snaps; e.coli beach closures

name: Big Sky
why: 5,800 acres and the Lone Peak Tram to 11,166 ft with the Big Couloir; among the largest and emptiest ski areas in the US.
heads_up: Expert tram terrain requires partner and beacon sign-out

name: Big White
why: Canada's largest ski-in/ski-out village, with reliable dry snow and the signature 'snow ghost' tree skiing.
heads_up: Frequent fog and flat light

name: Bighorn River
why: One of the highest trout-per-mile tailwaters in the country below Yellowtail Dam, fishable year-round with a dense lodge and guide community at Fort Smith.
heads_up: Very crowded on peak days; limited bank access on Crow Reservation land

name: Bird Island Basin
why: Padre Island National Seashore's 1-5 ft deep Laguna Madre, called the best flat-water windsurf site in the continental US, with an on-site concession school.
heads_up: Kiteboarding prohibited; separate day-use fee

name: Biscayne Bay / Coconut Grove
why: Winter racing capital of the US: the Bacardi Cup (since 1927), Olympic-class regattas and Coral Reef and Coconut Grove yacht clubs on flat, warm bay water.
heads_up: Shallow flats off the channels; summer heat and storms

name: Biscayne Bay / Virginia Key
why: Miami's SUP base, with Virginia Key Outdoor Center and clear flats paddling toward Key Biscayne.
heads_up: Afternoon thunderstorms in summer; boat channels

name: Bishop / Buttermilks
why: The Buttermilks, Happy and Sad Boulders make Bishop the most famous bouldering destination in North America, with the Owens River Gorge sport crag next door.
heads_up: Highball landings; winter wind and snow at 7,000 ft

name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison
why: The most serious traditional big-wall arena in the Lower 48, with committing routes and no bolts.
heads_up: Wilderness permit; poison ivy; no easy escape

name: Black Canyon Water Trail
why: A National Water Trail from Hoover Dam to Willow Beach with hot springs, Emerald Cave and no motors on Sundays and Mondays.
heads_up: Hoover Dam launch only via approved vendors; extreme summer heat

name: Black River (Watertown)
why: Warm, reliable summer flows and the Hole Brothers play spot make it the Northeast's most dependable summer class III-IV.
heads_up: Urban dams and low-head hazards upstream of the run

name: Black's Beach
why: The Scripps submarine canyon focuses swell into the most powerful beach break in Southern California.
heads_up: Steep cliff trail access; heavy barrels and rips; clothing-optional beach

name: Block Island
why: Block Island Race Week (Storm Trysail Club, biennial since 1965) fills Great Salt Pond with one of the East Coast's biggest fleets.
heads_up: Ferry logistics; fog

name: Blue Heron Bridge (Phil Foster Park)
why: Consistently ranked the best shore dive in the US for macro life and critters, with a dedicated snorkel trail and year-round diving.
heads_up: Dive only at slack high tide; boat channel nearby

name: Blue Hole
why: An 80-ft-deep bell-shaped artesian well with 100-ft visibility and constant 62F water that has been the Southwest's training and recreational dive magnet for decades.
heads_up: Permit required; 4,600 ft altitude; 20-diver limit

name: Boca de Pascuales
why: Mexico's other famous heavy beach break, a long-established tube-hunting destination with beachfront surf lodges.
heads_up: Powerful barrels and rips; strong currents at the rivermouth

name: Boca Grande Pass
why: The self-proclaimed Tarpon Capital of the World, where migrating tarpon stack in the pass each spring and tournaments date to the 1930s.
heads_up: A hundred boats in the pass on peak tides; strong currents

name: Boise Ridge to Rivers
why: 200+ miles of Ridge to Rivers foothills trail riding straight from downtown, plus Bogus Basin lift riding.
heads_up: Trails close when muddy; summer heat

name: Bonne Terre Mine
why: Billed as the world's largest freshwater dive resort, a billion-gallon flooded mine with 24 guided trails and 100-ft visibility that draws divers from across the country.
heads_up: Guided trails only, overhead environment, 58F water; one listing shows a temporary closure so confirm status before travelling

name: Bosque La Primavera
why: Protected forest on Guadalajara's edge with 250+ km of mapped trail and thousands of riders every weekend.
heads_up: Hot dry spring; navigation needed in a huge network

name: Boundary Waters Canoe Area
why: A million acres of linked lakes and portages, the most-visited wilderness in the US, with Ely's outfitters renting and permitting trips.
heads_up: Quota permits May-Sep; portages and bugs

name: Bow River
why: The world's best big-city trout river, with trophy browns and rainbows below Calgary and a long-established drift-boat guide scene.
heads_up: Flood years and runoff; long floats need shuttles; boat launches book up

name: Bowron Lake Canoe Circuit
why: A 116-km, 10-lake loop with portages taking six to ten days; reservations sell out the day they open and a mandatory orientation applies.
heads_up: Reservation required May 15-Sep 27; bears and portages

name: Breckenridge
why: Five peaks topping out at 12,998 ft, the highest chairlift in North America and one of the most-visited resorts in the US.
heads_up: Altitude sickness is common for arriving visitors

name: Bridger Bowl
why: The Ridge hike-to terrain and 'cold smoke' powder earned it a worldwide cult following among expert skiers.
heads_up: Ridge access requires avalanche transceiver

name: Brighton Beach (CIBBOWS)
why: Home of the Coney Island Brighton Beach Open Water Swimmers, New York's year-round ocean-swimming community with weekly group swims and the Grimaldo's Mile race.
heads_up: Cold winter water; lifeguard-season restrictions

name: Bristol Bay (King Salmon)
why: The largest sockeye run on earth and legendary rainbow rivers like the Kvichak, Naknek and Alagnak, served by the world's densest fly-out lodge network.
heads_up: Fly-in only; expensive lodges; bears and weather

name: Brockville / Thousand Islands
why: St. Lawrence River drift and wreck diving (Keystorm, Lillie Parsons, Daryaw) in warm, clear water that has supported a dive-charter community for decades.
heads_up: Strong river current; freighter traffic

name: Broken Group Islands
why: A hundred islands in Barkley Sound with Parks Canada campsites, the most-paddled multi-day sea-kayak destination in Canada.
heads_up: Fog, swell on outer islands, water-taxi from Toquart Bay

name: Bromont
venueType: lift-served bike park and trail network
why: Quebec's main lift-served bike park and former World Cup host, 45 minutes from Montreal with a large Eastern Townships trail network.
heads_up: Weekend crowds from Montreal

name: Brown County State Park
why: IMBA-endorsed 35-mile purpose-built network (Hobbs Hollow, Schooner Trace) that is the Midwest's flagship park ride.
heads_up: Park entry fee; clay trails close when wet

name: Browning Pass / God's Pocket
why: Browning Wall and the surrounding Emerald Sea sites are routinely called the best cold-water diving in the world, served by the God's Pocket dive resort.
heads_up: Strong tidal currents, slack-tide-only dives; remote

name: Bruce Peninsula (The Grotto / Bruce Trail)
why: The Grotto and the northern end of the 900 km Bruce Trail along Georgian Bay are Ontario's signature hikes.
heads_up: Timed parking reservations required at the Grotto

name: Bryce Canyon
why: The Navajo Loop and Queen's Garden through the hoodoos are the park's signature hikes, with the Fairyland and Peekaboo loops for longer days.
heads_up: Altitude (8,000 ft+); icy trails into May

name: Bucerias / Banderas Bay
why: Banderas Bay's afternoon thermal and the annual Festival del Viento (kite, wing and foil racing) make Bucerias the Pacific-mainland windsport base.
heads_up: Wind arrives after 1 pm; lighter than Baja

name: Buckskin Gulch & The Wave
why: Wire Pass trailhead serves both the longest slot canyon in the Southwest and the lottery-only Coyote Buttes North (The Wave).
heads_up: Wave lottery; flash floods in the slot

name: Buffalo National River (Upper)
why: America's first national river, with the Ponca-to-Kyles Landing float under 500-foot bluffs and a decades-old outfitter base.
heads_up: Upper river only floatable in spring; flash floods

name: Bugaboos
why: World-class alpine granite (Bugaboo Spire, Snowpatch, Becky-Chouinard on South Howser) based from the Conrad Kain Hut and Applebee camp.
heads_up: Glacier travel; rough access road; porcupines eat brake lines

name: Burlington / Lake Champlain
why: Lake Champlain's community sailing centre and yacht club host the Regatta for Lake Champlain and Etchells fleets, and the state-run Underwater Historic Preserves put moored canal boats, steamboats and the horse ferry within reach of divers.
heads_up: Sudden lake squalls; low visibility and cold water for divers

name: Cabo Pulmo
why: The only hard-coral reef in the Sea of Cortez and a conservation success story, with jack tornadoes, bull sharks and a village of dive co-ops.
heads_up: Dirt-road access; no-take park rules; surge in winter

name: Cabo San Lucas
why: The 'Marlin Capital of the World' (Bisbee's Black and Blue, Mexico's largest sportfishing fleet), finish of the Baja Ha-Ha cruisers' rally and a bay marine park (Pelican Rock, Sand Falls, Land's End) minutes from the marina.
heads_up: Hurricane season Aug-Oct; crowded marina; rough seas on the Pacific side

name: Cabrillo Beach (Hurricane Gulch)
why: LA's windiest beach, where the San Pedro Channel funnels the sea breeze to 20-30 knots; a windsurf and beach-cat venue since the 1970s.
heads_up: Offshore wind means a beat back; heavy ship traffic

name: Cache la Poudre
why: Colorado's only Wild & Scenic river, roadside class III-IV in Poudre Canyon with a rafting industry based in Fort Collins.
heads_up: Short snowmelt window; busy road shuttle

name: Campbell River
why: The 'Salmon Capital of the World' and home of Roderick Haig-Brown, with Tyee Club rowing tradition and Discovery Passage chinook, plus current-swept dive sites like Row and Be Damned with Steller sea lions.
heads_up: Strong tidal currents; changing DFO salmon closures

name: Canmore / Bow Valley
why: Grassi Lakes, Acephale and Lake Louise area crags make Canmore the hub of Canadian Rockies limestone sport climbing and Ha Ling / East End of Rundle hiking.
heads_up: Altitude and wildlife closures; trail fees at Nordic Centre

name: Canyonlands Needles District
why: The Chesler Park and Joint Trail loops from Elephant Hill are the classic Canyonlands backpacking circuits.
heads_up: Carry all water; backcountry permits

name: Cape Cod (Chatham / Monomoy)
why: Monomoy flats sight fishing for striped bass and the Cape Cod Canal are the Northeast's definitive striper destinations.
heads_up: Great white sharks near seal colonies; strong tides

name: Cape Hatteras / Buxton
why: The East Coast's premier surf destination, where hurricane and nor'easter swells meet the shifting sandbars below the lighthouse.
heads_up: Hurricane evacuations in season; 4WD for Cape Point; strong rips

name: Castle Mountain
why: Alberta's cult steep mountain: long fall-line chutes, Powder Stagecoach cat skiing and no crowds in the southern Rockies.
heads_up: Extreme wind; limited services

name: Catalina Channel
why: One of the Triple Crown of marathon swimming, 20 miles from Catalina to the mainland, sanctioned by the Catalina Channel Swimming Federation since 1927.
heads_up: Night start, cold water, escort boat and federation observer required

name: Catalina Island (Casino Point Dive Park)
why: The first underwater park in the US, with giant sea bass, garibaldi and kelp off a staircase entry in Avalon, plus a hyperbaric chamber on the island.
heads_up: Ferry access; crowded summer weekends

name: Cataract Canyon
why: Canyonlands' Big Drops reach class V at peak snowmelt; the standard multi-day Moab trip with permit from the park.
heads_up: Permit required; jet-boat or flight take-out from Lake Powell

name: Cathedral Ledge / North Conway
why: Cathedral and Whitehorse Ledges are the Northeast's granite multipitch training ground, backed by the White Mountains' hiking network.
heads_up: Summer crowds; polished classics

name: Catskills (Beaverkill / Willowemoc)
why: The birthplace of American dry-fly fishing, home to the Catskill Fly Fishing Center and the famous Junction Pool at 'Trout Town USA'.
heads_up: Warm low water in July and August; busy opening weeks

name: Cenote Dos Ojos
why: The gateway to the Yucatan's cenote cavern diving, with guided cavern lines (Barbie Line, Bat Cave) and snorkelling, part of the world's longest underwater cave system.
heads_up: Cavern guide ratios; full cave cert required beyond the lines

name: Cerritos Beach / Todos Santos
why: Southern Baja's most consistent learner beach, with on-sand surf schools and rentals and a swimmable sandy bottom.
heads_up: Afternoon crowds escaping north wind; faster at low tide

name: Channel Islands (Scorpion Anchorage)
why: National park and marine sanctuary with towering kelp forests, sea lions and Landing Cove on Anacapa, served by day boats from Ventura and Santa Barbara.
heads_up: Swell surges in caves; Santa Ana winds; open-ocean conditions

name: Charleston (Race Week)
why: Charleston Race Week is the largest keelboat regatta in the Americas (280+ boats), sailed in the harbour and offshore each April.
heads_up: Strong harbour tides; shoals

name: Chattanooga / Tennessee River Gorge
why: Home of Chattajack, the 31-mile endurance paddle through the Tennessee River Gorge held every October since 2012.
heads_up: Barge traffic; long distances with limited exits; PFD required

name: Chattooga River (Sections III & IV)
venueType: free-flowing class III-IV(V) Wild & Scenic river
why: Wild & Scenic river of Deliverance fame; Section III is a classic intermediate run and Section IV's Five Falls is a Southeastern class IV-V rite of passage.
heads_up: Undammed and rain-dependent; Five Falls has fatal sieves

name: Cheat River Canyon
why: Spring snowmelt run through a roadless canyon; home of Cheat Fest and a long-standing Appalachian rafting classic.
heads_up: Rain and snowmelt dependent; remote with no road access mid-canyon

name: Chelan Butte
why: Hosts the US Open of Paragliding and Chelan Open; DNR-managed butte with four designated launches and some of the best XC flying in North America.
heads_up: Dust devils and strong summer thermals; Lake Chelan Flyers membership and designated launches only; fire gear required in vehicles

name: Cherry Beach
why: Home water of the Toronto Windsurfing Club, Canada's largest windsurf club, with sheltered flats behind the Leslie Street Spit and city kite schools.
heads_up: Parking fills by 8:30 on weekends; gusty on strong SW

name: Chester (Mahone Bay)
why: Chester Race Week is Canada's largest keelboat regatta, with 1,300+ sailors on five courses in Mahone Bay each August.
heads_up: Fog and ledges among the islands

name: Chicago Harbor
why: Chicago Yacht Club's Race to Mackinac (since 1898) is the world's oldest annual freshwater distance race and starts off Navy Pier each July.
heads_up: Squalls on the lake; harbour slips scarce

name: Chilko River
why: Lava Canyon's 20 km of continuous class IV below Chilko Lake is the longest continuous whitewater in North America, run as multi-day trips.
heads_up: Remote fly-in or long gravel road; grizzly country

name: Chilkoot Trail
why: The Gold Rush route from Dyea over Chilkoot Pass into BC is a jointly managed US-Canada historic trail and classic multi-day backpack.
heads_up: Upper trail closed by flood damage, check NPS/Parks Canada status; permits

name: Chilliwack River
why: Tamihi and the canyon sections are Vancouver's go-to whitewater, with a long-running rafting and kayak-school scene an hour from the city.
heads_up: Cold snowmelt; busy road access on weekends

name: Cirque of the Towers / Wind River Range
why: Pingora and Wolf's Head draw alpine climbers from everywhere, and the Big Sandy to Cirque and Titcomb Basin routes are the Winds' legendary backpacks.
heads_up: Long rough access road; mosquitoes in July; grizzlies

name: City of Rocks
why: A national reserve of granite domes with 700+ bolted and trad routes, a classic moderate-grade destination since the 1980s.
heads_up: Remote; campsites book months ahead

name: Clark Fork Alberton Gorge
why: Warm big-water class III an hour from Missoula with Fang and Tumbleweed; the Montana summer play run.
heads_up: High June flows; Cyr bridge access only

name: Clayoquot Sound
why: Meares Island old-growth, Hot Springs Cove and grey whales from Tofino's long-established kayak outfitters.
heads_up: Open-coast exposure outside the inlets; fog

name: Clearwater River
why: Sabre Tooth and the Kettle at the gateway to Wells Gray Park, run commercially for decades from the town of Clearwater.
heads_up: Remote; high June flows

name: Cochise Stronghold
why: Southern Arizona's winter trad and multipitch dome climbing in the Dragoon Mountains.
heads_up: Seasonal raptor closures; remote dirt access

name: Cochrane
why: Calgary's training and ridge-soaring hill with the Alberta Hang Gliding and Paragliding Association and local schools.
heads_up: Wind-dependent ridge site; strong westerlies and gusty prairie conditions

name: Cocoa Beach
why: Kelly Slater's hometown and the East Coast surf capital, home to Ron Jon, the Cocoa Beach Surf Museum and numerous surf schools.
heads_up: Small, forgiving waves; pier crowds; summer flat spells

name: Columbia River Gorge (Eagle Creek)
why: Eagle Creek to Tunnel Falls, Multnomah-Wahkeena and Dog Mountain are the Gorge's landmark waterfall and wildflower hikes.
heads_up: Timed-use permits at Multnomah in season; exposed ledges

name: Copper Canyon (Barrancas del Cobre)
why: Deeper than the Grand Canyon, with multi-day treks from Divisadero and Creel into Rarámuri villages via the Chepe railway.
heads_up: Unmarked trails, hire a local guide; cold nights at the rim

name: Copper Harbor
why: IMBA Ride Center at the tip of the Keweenaw with 70+ miles of rocky, bermed singletrack and the Copper Harbor Trails Fest.
heads_up: Remote; short season and bugs in June

name: Copper Mountain
why: Naturally divided terrain, US Ski Team early-season speed centre and the Woodward park make it a core Summit County destination.
heads_up: I-70 weekend traffic from Denver

name: Costa Azul / Zippers
why: Los Cabos' signature right point, the East Cape's summer swell magnet with resort-side surf schools and the Zippers break.
heads_up: Crowded and localised; rocky; hurricane season swells

name: Coyote Point
why: Historic Bay Area windsurf beach with steady summer sea breeze and the Peninsula's long-running windsurf community.
heads_up: County park entry fee; shallow at low tide

name: Cozumel (Palancar / Santa Rosa Wall)
why: One of the top five dive destinations in the world: Palancar, Santa Rosa Wall and Columbia in a marine park, with over 100 dive operators.
heads_up: Drift diving in current; cruise-ship days are crowded

name: Crandon Park, Key Biscayne
why: Miami's kite beach, run as a concession with IKO-level requirements, huge shallow flats inside the reef and winter fronts for wind.
heads_up: Certification, helmet and pennant required; west wind not recommended

name: Crested Butte
why: Extreme Limits terrain gave birth to US freeskiing competition, and the town is the home of the Mountain Bike Hall of Fame with alpine classics 401, Doctor Park and Teocalli Ridge.
heads_up: High altitude; snow lingers on upper trails into July

name: Crissy Field
why: Sailing under the Golden Gate in 25-knot summer sea breeze and ebb-tide swell is a bucket-list session; the San Francisco Boardsailing Association has defended access here for decades.
heads_up: Ebb tide can sweep you out the Gate; cold water, shipping lane

name: Crown Beach, Alameda
why: The Bay Area's beginner beach: waist-deep water for hundreds of metres and the region's main kite and windsurf schools based on the sand.
heads_up: Very shallow at low tide; mud

name: Crystal Mountain
why: Washington's largest ski area with a gondola, Mount Rainier views and Southback inbounds backcountry.
heads_up: Heavy Cascade snow and weekend Seattle crowds

name: Crystal River / Three Sisters Springs
why: The only place in the US where you can legally snorkel with wild manatees, with dozens of licensed operators inside Crystal River National Wildlife Refuge.
heads_up: Strict no-touch rules and seasonal closures; cold mornings

name: Cumberland
why: Vancouver Island's signature trail town with a large United Riders of Cumberland network on forestry land right from the village.
heads_up: Trails on private forestry land; respect closures and logging activity

name: Cuyuna Lakes
why: IMBA Ride Center built on red-dirt mine tailings with 70+ miles of flow trail and dedicated bike lodging in Crosby-Ironton.
heads_up: Mosquitoes in June; fat-bike groomed in winter

name: Dana Point / Doheny
why: The spiritual home of SUP racing, where the Battle of the Paddle and Pacific Paddle Games ran at Doheny State Beach, with daily paddling from Baby Beach in the harbor.
heads_up: SUP prohibited at Doheny main beach outside event days; paddle from the harbor

name: Davidson River
why: Pisgah National Forest river consistently ranked among Trout Unlimited's top 100, with a hatchery-supported fly-only catch-and-release section.
heads_up: Highly pressured, educated fish; fly-only regs on the lower river

name: Dean River
why: Fly-in-only river with the hardest-fighting summer steelhead in the world, run through a handful of historic lodges below the falls.
heads_up: Floatplane access only; lottery and classified-water limits; bears

name: Deep Cove
why: Metro Vancouver's most established SUP launch, with Deep Cove Kayak rentals and lessons and Indian Arm fjord routes.
heads_up: Very busy summer weekends; afternoon inflow wind

name: Deer Valley
why: Perennially top-ranked groomed-snow resort with capped daily ticket sales and a pioneering lift-served bike park.
heads_up: Skiers only in winter; expensive

name: Deerfield River (Fife Brook / Dryway)
why: Scheduled releases give a beginner Fife Brook section and the class IV Dryway, with Zoar Outdoor and other schools based in Charlemont.
heads_up: Release schedule dependent; Dryway is class IV

name: Denali
why: North America's highest peak and the West Buttress is the continent's defining expedition climb, flown in from Talkeetna.
heads_up: NPS permit 60 days ahead; extreme cold and altitude

name: Deschutes River
why: Native redside rainbows, a legendary May salmonfly hatch and a summer steelhead run make the lower Deschutes a bucket-list Western river.
heads_up: No fishing from boats; boater pass required; strong current and rattlesnakes

name: Desolation Canyon (Green River)
why: Eighty-four miles of class II-III through a canyon deeper than the Grand, the standard beginner-friendly multi-day in Utah.
heads_up: BLM permit; remote Sand Wash launch on dirt road

name: Desolation Sound
why: BC's largest marine park, with the warmest ocean water north of Mexico and outfitters in Lund and Powell River.
heads_up: Summer boat traffic; limited fresh water

name: Devil's Den
why: A prehistoric spring inside a dry cave, run as a dedicated dive resort and one of the most-photographed training and recreational dive sites in the US.
heads_up: Snorkelling by reservation only; certified divers only below the surface

name: Devils Tower
why: America's first national monument is a bucket-list crack-climbing tower with over 200 routes.
heads_up: Voluntary June closure for Native ceremonies; register at visitor center

name: Donner Lake
why: The Donner Lake Swim, a 2.7-mile crossing run since 1980 and one of the most sought-after USMS open-water races, sells out in hours.
heads_up: 5,900 ft altitude; cool water; lottery-speed registration

name: Door County (Cave Point)
why: Cave Point's limestone caves and shipwreck tours make Door County the Lake Michigan kayak destination with several outfitters.
heads_up: Cold water; caves unsafe in onshore swell

name: Downieville
why: The 17-mile, 4,400 ft Downieville Downhill and the Downieville Classic race made it a West Coast institution.
heads_up: Shuttle required; rocky, exposed and remote

name: Driftless Area
why: Thousands of miles of restored limestone spring creeks with wild browns and brookies, a Trout Unlimited showcase and a growing fly-tourism economy.
heads_up: Private land with public easements; tall grass and ticks

name: Dry Tortugas
why: National park 70 miles west of Key West with the healthiest reefs in the Keys, the Windjammer wreck and snorkelling right off Fort Jefferson.
heads_up: Access only by ferry, seaplane or liveaboard; limited daily visitors

name: Duluth / Spirit Mountain
venueType: lift-served bike park and trail network
why: IMBA Gold-level Ride Center with the 100-mile Duluth Traverse and a lift-served park at Spirit Mountain.
heads_up: Rocky Lake Superior terrain; cool and windy

name: Duluth / Stoney Point
why: Lake Superior's signature point break and the centre of the North Shore surf community, famed for ice-beard winter sessions.
heads_up: Water near 0 C; only works on strong NE gales; rocky entry

name: Dunlap
why: Sierra foothill thermal and XC site with reliable spring conditions, a dedicated LZ and a long competition history.
heads_up: Hot, strong summer thermals; private LZ fee

name: DuPont State Forest
why: 83 miles of granite-slab and flow trails (Ridgeline, Cedar Rock) that pair with Pisgah to make Brevard a riding town.
heads_up: Crowded parking lots on weekends

name: Durango
why: Host of the first UCI MTB World Championships (1990) and home of Ned Overend, with Horse Gulch and Hermosa Creek riding from town.
heads_up: Altitude; some high trails hold snow until June

name: Duthie Hill / Tiger Mountain
why: Evergreen MTB Alliance's flagship Duthie Hill jump park and the Tiger Mountain descents anchor Seattle-area riding.
heads_up: Crowded weekends; mud in winter

name: Edgartown
why: Edgartown Race Weekend and the Round-the-Island race draw big fleets to Martha's Vineyard each July.
heads_up: Strong harbour currents; ferry access

name: Edmonds Underwater Park
why: A 27-acre protected underwater park with 2.5 miles of marked trails and sunken structures beside the ferry dock, the most-dived site in Puget Sound.
heads_up: Low visibility, compass navigation; evening permit after dark

name: El Cruce (Cancun to Isla Mujeres)
why: Mexico's biggest open-water event, a 10 km crossing from Playa Caracol to Isla Mujeres over the MUSA museum that draws 1,500-plus swimmers and ranks in the World's Top 100.
heads_up: Open-sea current and chop; 1.9 and 3.8 km options for shorter distances

name: El Cuyo
why: Yucatan's most consistent kite beach (18-23 kn spring thermals, 180+ windy days) with a growing school scene and the El Cuyo Kite Fest.
heads_up: Remote village; wind builds after 1 pm

name: El Potrero Chico
why: Mexico's most famous crag, with 600+ bolted routes including 20-pitch limestone classics like Time Wave Zero, and a full winter climber scene.
heads_up: Loose rock on long routes; heat outside winter

name: Eldorado Canyon / Boulder
why: Eldo's steep Fountain sandstone (Bastille Crack, Naked Edge) plus the Flatirons and Boulder Canyon make Boulder a year-round climbing capital.
heads_up: Timed-entry vehicle reservations in season; runout classics

name: Elk River
why: Westslope cutthroat on dry flies all summer in a classified BC river with a strong guide and lodge community in Fernie.
heads_up: Classified-water licence and guided-day rules for non-residents; runoff until July

name: Ellenville
why: The Northeast's most-flown mountain site on the Shawangunk Ridge, with schools, tandems, the Southern New York Hang Gliding Club and a dedicated LZ.
heads_up: Site membership and sign-in; strong northwest days are rowdy

name: Ensenada
why: Finish of the Newport-to-Ensenada race, with the Hotel Coral marina fiesta hosting 150+ boats every April since 1948.
heads_up: Customs/immigration clearance for arriving yachts

name: Everglades (Flamingo)
why: Everglades National Park's backcountry offers the classic snook, redfish and tarpon skiff fishery out of Flamingo marina.
heads_up: Mosquitoes and heat; navigation in shallow backcountry; park permits

name: Everglades Wilderness Waterway
why: The 99-mile marked trail from Everglades City to Flamingo through the Ten Thousand Islands, with chickee platforms and backcountry permits.
heads_up: Winter only (bugs, heat); navigation and tides in mangroves

name: Fat Salmon (Lake Washington)
why: The Pacific Northwest's largest USMS open-water race, from the I-90 bridge to Madison Park Beach, with Lake Washington swum year-round by Seattle clubs.
heads_up: Two-hour cut-off; cool water, boat traffic

name: Fernie
why: Five alpine bowls and about 30 feet of snow a season in a historic coal town with a strong trail network for summer.
heads_up: Deep-snow tree wells; weather-related alpine closures

name: Floras Lake
why: A sandy-bottom freshwater lake a dune away from the Pacific with 15-25 kn NW wind and a long-running windsports school; the Oregon coast's learning spot.
heads_up: Wind arrives midday; nearest services are small

name: Flower Garden Banks
why: The northernmost coral reefs in the continental US, a National Marine Sanctuary 100 miles offshore reached by liveaboard, famous for the August mass coral spawn and manta rays.
heads_up: Liveaboard only, 60-110 ft dives, rough Gulf crossings

name: Fogland Beach
why: The Sakonnet River cove is one of the windiest spots in Rhode Island and the state's long-standing windsurf and kite launch.
heads_up: Non-resident parking fee; little swell

name: Folly Beach / The Washout
why: The Southeast's established surf town, with the Washout as its signature peak and a dense cluster of surf shops and schools.
heads_up: Tide-dependent; summer small; hurricane swells can close roads

name: Foster Falls / South Cumberland
why: Foster Falls, Denny Cove and the Tennessee Wall anchor Chattanooga's reputation as the Southeast's sandstone climbing hub.
heads_up: Daily online climbing registration; humid summers

name: French Broad (Section 9)
why: Frank Bell's Rapid and a dependable year-round flow make Section 9 the Asheville area's standard rafting and kayaking run.
heads_up: Flashes high after rain; cold water in spring

name: Fruita / Grand Junction
why: 18 Road, Kokopelli Loops and the Lunch Loops are a spring and fall desert staple with the Fruita Fat Tire Festival since 1996.
heads_up: Exposure on Horsethief Bench; heat in summer

name: Fryingpan River
why: Gold Medal tailwater below Ruedi Reservoir famous for the 'Toilet Bowl' trophy trout and mysis shrimp, with a fly-shop culture in Basalt.
heads_up: Tiny flies and technical fish; limited public access; winter cold

name: Galbraith Mountain
why: 65+ miles of WMBC-built singletrack minutes from downtown; widely rated Washington's best trail system.
heads_up: Wet and rooty in winter; shared with hikers

name: Gallatin River
why: The Mad Mile and House Rock in Gallatin Canyon are Montana's standard day run, with outfitters lining US 191 between Big Sky and Bozeman.
heads_up: Cold snowmelt; low by August

name: Garibaldi / Panorama Ridge
why: Garibaldi Lake, Panorama Ridge and Black Tusk from Rubble Creek are the Sea-to-Sky's definitive big day hikes.
heads_up: Day-use passes and camping reservations; 30 km round trip to the ridge

name: Gaspé Rivers (York / Dartmouth / Saint-Jean)
why: Crystal-clear sight-fishing rivers for large Atlantic salmon, managed by the ZEC Gaspé with lottery pools since the 1970s.
heads_up: Pool lottery and daily draws; clear water demands stealth

name: Gates of Lodore (Green River)
why: Dinosaur National Monument's red-walled canyon with Hell's Half Mile; permit lottery and a classic family multi-day.
heads_up: Permit lottery; cold Flaming Gorge release water

name: Gauley River (Upper & Lower)
why: Six to seven weeks of scheduled Summersville Dam releases after Labor Day create the Upper Gauley's five class V rapids and the annual Gauley Fest, the largest paddling festival in the world.
heads_up: Release weekends only; Upper is class V with mandatory swims consequences

name: Georgian Bay (30,000 Islands)
why: The world's largest freshwater archipelago, with Killbear and Massasauga parks and the Georgian Bay Coast water trail from Parry Sound outfitters.
heads_up: Sudden squalls on open bay; rattlesnakes on islands

name: Ghost Lake
why: Calgary's wind lake: a deep reservoir on the Bow with steady westerlies, a sailing academy and Alberta's main kite and windsurf community.
heads_up: Very cold water; rocky shore

name: Gilboa Quarry
why: The Midwest's best-known purpose-run dive quarry, with a sunken airliner, platforms and a 130-ft deep side used for recreational and technical training.
heads_up: Cold below the thermocline; weekend crowds

name: Ginnie Springs
why: The flagship of Florida's cave-diving country: 72F crystal water year-round, the Ballroom cavern open to recreational divers and the Devil's system for certified cave divers.
heads_up: Cave penetration requires cave certification; crowded on weekends

name: Glacier Bay
why: Tour-boat kayak drop-offs from Bartlett Cove to the upper-bay tidewater glaciers, with free backcountry permits and orientation.
heads_up: 25-foot tides, brown bears, mandatory orientation May-Sep

name: Glacier National Park (Highline Trail)
why: The Highline Trail from Logan Pass, Grinnell Glacier and Iceberg Lake are among the most photographed hikes in the Rockies.
heads_up: Vehicle reservations; grizzly country, carry spray

name: Golden (Mount 7)
why: Canada's premier XC site, 1,200 m above the Columbia Valley, host of the Canadian Nationals and the Willi Muller XC Challenge.
heads_up: Strong thermals and long glides into a narrow valley; FSR drive to launch; landing restrictions

name: Grand Canyon (Bright Angel / South Kaibab)
why: Rim-to-river and rim-to-rim on the Bright Angel and Kaibab trails are America's most famous canyon hikes, with Phantom Ranch at the bottom.
heads_up: Extreme inner-canyon heat; backcountry permits by lottery

name: Grand Canyon (Colorado River)
why: The world's most sought-after river trip: 226 miles from Lees Ferry with Lava Falls and Crystal, allocated by weighted lottery or commercial outfitters.
heads_up: Private permits via lottery years ahead; commercial trips book 1-2 years out

name: Grand Haven
why: Birthplace of Lake Michigan kiteboarding and home of MACkite and the King of the Great Lakes event; works on everything but east wind.
heads_up: Summer beach crowds often close the launch; cold water

name: Grand River (Fergus)
why: Ontario's premier brown-trout tailwater below Shand Dam, with a dedicated fly-only stretch and a strong Toronto-area guide and shop scene.
heads_up: Warm late-summer water; special regs on the tailwater

name: Grand Targhee
why: Roughly 500 inches of consistent Teton snowfall on the quiet west side of the range with lift-served powder and cat skiing.
heads_up: Frequent storm-day whiteouts; remote access via Teton Pass or Idaho

name: Grand Teton
why: The Grand's Exum and Owen-Spalding ridges are the classic American alpine climbs, and Cascade Canyon and the Teton Crest Trail are landmark hikes.
heads_up: Backcountry permits; afternoon lightning

name: Great Bear Lake
why: Holds nearly every lake trout world record and hosts legendary fly-in lodges such as Plummer's since the 1960s.
heads_up: Fly-in only, short season; expensive; arctic weather

name: Great Chesapeake Bay Swim
why: A lottery-entry 4.4-mile crossing between the spans of the Bay Bridge every second Sunday of June, one of the most iconic US open-water events.
heads_up: Strong tides, 40-minute-per-mile pace cut-off, lottery entry

name: Great Smoky Mountains (Alum Cave / AT)
why: The most-visited national park in the US, with Alum Cave to Mt LeConte, Charlies Bunion and 70 miles of the Appalachian Trail.
heads_up: Parking tag required; summer haze and crowds

name: Green River (Flaming Gorge)
why: Red-rock canyon tailwater below Flaming Gorge Dam with gin-clear water, sight fishing and some of the highest trout densities in the US.
heads_up: Crowds on the A section; shuttle logistics; cicada hatch frenzy in June

name: Green River Narrows
why: Scheduled Tuxedo powerhouse releases make this the most-run class V in North America and host of the Green Race each November.
heads_up: Expert-only; Gorilla and Sunshine have taken lives; long hike-in

name: Gros Morne / Bonne Bay
why: Bonne Bay's fjord arms beneath the Tablelands, with guided paddles from Norris Point inside Gros Morne National Park.
heads_up: Cold water and katabatic wind off the fjord walls

name: Gros Morne National Park
why: The Gros Morne Mountain summit loop, Western Brook Pond fjord and the Long Range Traverse are Atlantic Canada's premier hikes.
heads_up: Summit trail closed in spring for caribou calving; traverse requires navigation test

name: Guadalcázar
why: Gruta de las Candelas, San Cayetano and Salitre offer Mexico's best stalactite-cave sport climbing, with local guiding and a growing route count.
heads_up: Respect the small town; wet season Nov–Feb

name: Guadalupe Peak
why: The Texas high point and McKittrick Canyon's fall color draw hikers to Guadalupe Mountains National Park.
heads_up: High winds; no water on trail

name: Gwaii Haanas
why: Two days' paddle from Moresby Camp to SGang Gwaay's Haida poles; Parks Canada says it is not for novices and runs a reservation and orientation system.
heads_up: Trip permit, mandatory orientation, logging-road access, exposed water

name: Habitat 67 (Montreal river wave)
why: North America's best-known standing river wave on the St. Lawrence, with a 20-year community and KSF school and rentals.
heads_up: Strong current and eddy lines; cold spring water; queue etiquette

name: Haida Gwaii (Langara Island)
why: Langara Island's fly-in lodges sit on the migration route of the largest chinook in the Pacific, a destination salmon fishery since the 1980s.
heads_up: Fly-in lodges only; open ocean swell; DFO chinook limits

name: Haines
why: Three borough-permitted heli operators and the Takhinsha spines made famous by countless ski and snowboard films.
heads_up: Heli-ski only; weather down days are common

name: Haleakalā (Sliding Sands)
why: The Sliding Sands to Halemauʻu crater traverse is Maui's landmark high-altitude hike.
heads_up: Altitude (10,000 ft); sunrise entry reservations

name: Haleakala / Polipoli (Maui)
why: Proflyght Paragliding has flown Haleakala's upcountry slopes for decades with morning glass-off flights of 3,000 ft vertical.
heads_up: Early-morning window only before trade winds; rough access road

name: Halifax (Northwest Arm)
why: Home of the Royal Nova Scotia Yacht Squadron (1837), the Marblehead-to-Halifax Ocean Race finish and Atlantic Canada's main racing fleets.
heads_up: Fog; cold Atlantic water

name: Hanalei Bay
why: Kauai's premier surf bay with multiple reef breaks, long-running surf schools, and flatwater SUP on the Hanalei River.
heads_up: Big winter swells; limited parking; river mouth runoff after rain

name: Hanauma Bay
why: Hawaii's first Marine Life Conservation District and its most famous snorkel bay, with reservations, an education centre and shallow reef inside a flooded crater.
heads_up: Advance reservation; closed Mondays and Tuesdays; crowds

name: Hapuna Roughwater Swim
why: The Big Island's premier open-water race, the middle leg of the Kona Triple Crown swim series at Hapuna Beach State Park.
heads_up: Shorebreak at Hapuna; in-water mass start

name: Harding Icefield Trail
why: The 8.2-mile climb from Exit Glacier to the Harding Icefield is Alaska's most accessible and iconic day hike in Kenai Fjords.
heads_up: Bears on trail; snow on upper section into July

name: Hardwood Ski and Bike
why: Host of the 2015 Pan Am Games mountain biking and Ontario's established XC race and trail centre an hour north of Toronto.
heads_up: Trail pass required; rolling XC rather than big descents

name: Hatcher Pass
why: Alaska's most-flown mountain site with drive-up launches at Summit Lake and Marmot Mountain, flown by the Arctic Air Walkers club.
heads_up: Road open roughly June to September; remote rescue; mountain weather

name: Hatteras Island – Canadian Hole / Kite Point
why: The Pamlico Sound side of Cape Hatteras is the East Coast's windsport mecca: waist-deep flats at Canadian Hole and Kite Point with ocean waves across the road.
heads_up: Nor'easters and hurricanes; shallow sound at low water

name: Havasupai (Havasu Falls)
why: The 10-mile trek from Hualapai Hilltop to the turquoise waterfalls of Havasu Canyon is one of the most sought-after permits in North America.
heads_up: Tribal permits sell out instantly; flash floods

name: Heavenly
why: 4,800 acres straddling California and Nevada with Lake Tahoe views and Mott and Killebrew canyon steeps.
heads_up: Crowded gondola; casino-town base

name: Henry's Fork (Railroad Ranch)
why: The most famous technical dry-fly water in America, with the Harriman Ranch section opening June 15 and world-class PMD and green drake hatches.
heads_up: Selective, educated rainbows; Ranch opens June 15; mosquitoes

name: Highland Mountain Bike Park
why: The only bike-only lift-served mountain in North America, known for progression trails, jump lines and coaching.
heads_up: Day passes sell out on weekends

name: Ho'okipa Beach Park
why: The most famous wave-sailing arena on earth, home to the Aloha Classic and the sport's pro community since the early 1980s.
heads_up: Experts only; shallow reef, strong current, surfers have priority before 11 am

name: Holbox
why: Car-free island with IKO kite schools on the standing-depth flats at Playa Las Nubes since 2005, and the Yucatan's giant migratory tarpon fishery with 100-plus pound fish offshore each summer.
heads_up: Ferry access; unreliable wind in late summer; summer rain and hurricane season for tarpon

name: Homestead Crater
why: A 65-ft-deep 90F hot spring inside a 55-ft limestone dome, the only warm scuba site in the Rockies and a year-round certification venue.
heads_up: Reservations required; silty bottom; 5,600 ft altitude

name: Honolua Bay
why: Maui's crown-jewel right point and a long-time WSL Women's Championship Tour venue.
heads_up: Sharp reef and cliff-trail access; needs a solid NW swell

name: Honolulu / Ala Wai (Transpac finish)
why: Finish of the biennial Transpacific Yacht Race off Diamond Head, with Waikiki and Hawaii yacht clubs hosting the fleet at the Ala Wai.
heads_up: Trade-wind chop outside the harbour

name: Hood River / The Gorge
why: The Columbia Gorge's thermal westerlies against the river current made Hood River the windsurfing capital of the world in the 1980s and it remains the mainland hub for kite, wing and foil brands, schools and events.
heads_up: Strong current and barge traffic; nukes to 30+ kn on big days; leash and PFD for downwinders

name: Hopewell Rocks / Bay of Fundy
why: Paddling among the flowerpot rocks at high tide with the world's highest tides, run by the sole licensed outfitter inside the park.
heads_up: Tide-timed tours only; 40-foot tidal range

name: Horseshoe Canyon Ranch
why: A private Ozark dude ranch with 400+ routes and the 24 Hours of Horseshoe Hell festival.
heads_up: Private land; check in and pay at the Trading Post

name: Horsetooth Reservoir
why: Host of the Horsetooth Swims since 1999, the Rocky Mountain region's established open-water race (10K, 2.4 and 1.2 miles) at 5,430 ft.
heads_up: Altitude; 62-70F water; boat traffic outside race days

name: Hudson River Gorge
why: Scheduled Indian River releases feed a 17-mile Adirondack gorge run that has supported rafting outfitters since the 1980s.
heads_up: Cold snowmelt in April; long day with no mid-run exit

name: Hueco Tanks
why: The birthplace of the V-grade and one of the world's great bouldering areas inside a Texas state park.
heads_up: Daily reservations; guided access only beyond North Mountain

name: Huntington Beach
why: Trademarked 'Surf City USA', host of the US Open of Surfing and the International Surfing Museum.
heads_up: Large crowds and strong summer rips near the pier

name: Hurricane / St. George (Gooseberry Mesa)
why: Gooseberry Mesa, JEM, Little Creek and Zen make this the winter desert riding hub of southwest Utah.
heads_up: Rough dirt access roads; cliff-edge exposure on mesa trails

name: Index
why: The Lower Town Wall is Washington's premier granite trad crag, famous for steep, technical cracks.
heads_up: Wet rock much of the year; stiff grades

name: Indian Creek
why: The world's best crack climbing, with thousands of perfectly parallel sandstone splitters in Bears Ears.
heads_up: Bring many cams per size; no water; dispersed camping rules

name: Invermere (Mount Swansea)
why: Columbia Valley site with drive-up launch, a lakeside LZ and a long club history, often paired with Golden on XC trips.
heads_up: Strong valley thermals; FSR access

name: Isla Blanca
why: The Chacmuchuc lagoon north of Cancun is the Riviera Maya's safest learning spot: flat, waist-deep water and steady Nortes and trades November to June.
heads_up: Rough dirt road; wetsuit on Norte days

name: Isla Espíritu Santo
why: Beach-camping circumnavigation of Espíritu Santo with sea lions at Los Islotes; overnight trips run October to May from La Paz.
heads_up: Afternoon wind on the crossing; bugs Oct-Nov on mangrove beaches

name: Isla Mujeres (whale sharks, MUSA)
why: The largest whale-shark aggregation on the planet gathers off Isla Mujeres each summer, and the MUSA underwater sculpture museum sits in the Cancun marine park year-round.
heads_up: Licensed boats only, snorkel-only with whale sharks; early departures

name: Islamorada
venueType: Keys flats, reef and sound-side launch
why: The 'Sport Fishing Capital of the World' and birthplace of flats fly fishing, the Keys' flagship kite and wing launch at Whale Harbor (Wind Games), and Alligator Reef and the Eagle wreck for divers, all from one town.
heads_up: Guides book a year ahead; tight kite launch with $10 fee; current on the Eagle

name: Isle Royale
why: The Greenstone Ridge is the classic 40-mile traverse of the least-visited national park, and ten major wrecks (Emperor, America, Kamloops) make it the finest cold-water wreck diving in the Great Lakes.
heads_up: Ferry or seaplane access only; dive permit from the park; near-freezing water

name: Iztaccíhuatl
why: The La Joya route up Izta is Mexico's most-climbed high peak and acclimatisation standard, with Paso de Cortés trails below.
heads_up: Road closures during Popocatépetl eruptions; altitude

name: Jacks Canyon
why: Northern Arizona's densely bolted limestone canyon with hundreds of moderate sport routes and free camping at the rim.
heads_up: Access road becomes impassable mud after rain

name: Jackson Hole
why: 4,139 ft of continuous vertical, Corbet's Couloir and a tram-served alpine with open-gate backcountry make it North America's benchmark big-mountain resort; the same tram serves a 4,000 ft paragliding launch in summer.
heads_up: Steep terrain and serious avalanche exposure beyond the gates; summer tram season only for flying

name: Jacques-Cartier River
why: The Tewkesbury section is Quebec City's established spring rafting run, with the Valcartier outfitter base since the 1980s.
heads_up: Spring-only flows; cold snowmelt

name: Jay Peak
why: The East's snowiest resort (around 350 inches) with the region's best glade skiing and an aerial tram.
heads_up: Wind and extreme cold near the border

name: Jericho / English Bay
why: Jericho Sailing Centre is Canada's largest community sailing and windsurfing centre, next door to the Royal Vancouver Yacht Club and English Bay's regatta courses.
heads_up: Light summer winds except on westerlies; freighter anchorage

name: Jetty Island
why: Puget Sound's premier kite spot: warm shallow flats on the west side with afternoon NW thermals, famous enough to make TheKiteMag's global travel list.
heads_up: Paddle across the channel with gear; bird refuge, no dogs

name: Johnstone Strait / Telegraph Cove
why: Northern resident orcas at the Robson Bight reserve make Johnstone Strait the world's best-known orca kayaking, with base camps run from Telegraph Cove.
heads_up: Strong currents, cruise-ship wake, cold water

name: Jordan River / Sombrio
why: Vancouver Island's south-coast point break, the original Victoria-area surf spot with a long local history.
heads_up: Only works on big westerly swells; limited parking; cold water

name: Joshua Tree
why: Over 8,000 routes and boulder problems across a national park; the defining winter trad and bouldering destination in the US.
heads_up: Campgrounds fill fast; summer is dangerously hot

name: Jupiter
why: The Gulf Stream drift-diving capital of the US, famous for the goliath grouper aggregation every late summer and lemon shark season in winter.
heads_up: Strong current, live-boat drift only; sharks

name: K-38 / Rosarito
why: The classic Baja Norte weekend wave for Southern California surfers, a cobblestone reef point at kilometre 38 with rentals and lodging on site.
heads_up: Rocky entry; border wait times; variable water quality

name: Kagel Mountain / Sylmar
why: Home of the Sylmar Hang Gliding Association, one of the oldest free-flight clubs in the country, with a club LZ and shuttles.
heads_up: SHGA membership and site intro required; strong summer thermals

name: Kahana Bay
why: The Hawaii Paragliding Association's most-flown trade-wind site on Oahu's windward coast, with hike-up launches and beach landings.
heads_up: USHPA and HPA membership required; hike-up launch; trade winds can overpower

name: Kailua Beach
why: Oahu's windsport hub: steady trades over a sandy bay with multiple schools and rental outfits teaching kite, wing and windsurf from the same beach, plus the classic paddle out to the Mokulua islets.
heads_up: Launch zones regulated; trades push offshore; no landing on Moku Nui's back side

name: Kalmus Beach
why: Measured as the windiest spot north of Hatteras, Kalmus has a dedicated windsurf zone and 15-20 kn SW summer sea breeze.
heads_up: Kiting only after 4 pm in season; paid parking

name: Kamloops Bike Ranch
why: Birthplace of freeride (Kranked films) with Canada's largest municipal bike park and desert-style trails on Pineview, Lac du Bois and Harper.
heads_up: Very hot and dry in July-August; loose soil

name: Kanaha Beach Park (Kite Beach)
why: Year-round side-onshore trades and a reef-protected lagoon make Kanaha the world's best-known kite and windsurf learning beach, with 100+ sailors out on a normal day.
heads_up: No kiting/windsurfing before 11 am; crowded launch

name: Kananaskis River
why: Canoe Meadows and the Widowmaker course, with scheduled Barrier Dam releases, are Alberta's teaching and slalom venue an hour from Calgary.
heads_up: Release-schedule dependent; cold mountain water

name: Katahdin / Baxter State Park
why: The Knife Edge and the northern terminus of the Appalachian Trail make Katahdin Maine's must-do mountain.
heads_up: Day-use parking reservations; alpine exposure

name: Kealakekua Bay
why: Paddling across to the Captain Cook Monument and its reef is the Big Island's signature kayak-and-snorkel trip, run by state-permitted operators.
heads_up: State permit required to land; spinner-dolphin protections

name: Keho Lake
why: Southern Alberta's chinook-fed reservoir with multiple named launches (Kite Beach, Speed Beach, Wave Beach) and 60 km/h-plus days several times a month.
heads_up: Gusty chinooks; shoreline parking rules

name: Kelly Park, Banana River
why: An internationally recognised windsurf lagoon on the Banana River with dedicated sailboard launch; kite schools in Cocoa Beach use the same shallow water with boat support.
heads_up: Kite launch through trees is intermediate+ only; onshore SE wind needed

name: Kemah / Galveston Bay
why: The Gulf Coast's largest sailing fleet, based at Clear Lake/Kemah with the Harvest Moon Regatta and Lakewood and Houston yacht clubs.
heads_up: Shallow bay, summer heat and storms

name: Kenai Fjords
why: Water-taxi drops to Aialik Bay and Bear Glacier Lagoon put paddlers under calving tidewater glaciers; Seward hosts a mature guide and water-taxi industry.
heads_up: Exposed Gulf of Alaska coast; afternoon surf at landings

name: Kenai River
why: Home of the world-record king salmon and Alaska's most accessible salmon and trophy-rainbow fishery, with a huge guide fleet.
heads_up: Combat fishing at the sockeye peak; shifting king closures; bears

name: Kennebec River (The Forks)
why: Daily Harris Station releases through the Kennebec Gorge, plus the nearby Dead River's high-volume release days, make The Forks New England's rafting capital.
heads_up: Big-water hydraulics at Magic Falls; cold water early season

name: Kern River
why: Lower, Upper and Forks of the Kern give everything from family floats to the class V Forks wilderness run, all based from Kernville.
heads_up: Kern has a deadly reputation at high water; Forks requires permit and pack-in

name: Key Largo / John Pennekamp (Molasses Reef, Christ of the Abyss)
why: Self-styled Dive Capital of the World: the only living coral barrier reef in the continental US, dozens of dive shops, Molasses Reef, the Spiegel Grove wreck and the Christ of the Abyss statue inside Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary.
heads_up: Crowded moorings on weekends; afternoon summer squalls

name: Key West (USNS Vandenberg)
why: The 523-ft Vandenberg, sunk in 2009, is one of the largest artificial reefs in the world and anchors Key West's established wreck-diving scene alongside Sand Key and the Cayman Salvager.
heads_up: Deck at 100 ft; currents on the wreck

name: Kicking Horse / Golden
why: Champagne-powder bowls, 85 inbounds chutes and the highest proportion of expert terrain of any Canadian resort, plus gondola-served downhill and the Mount 7 and Moonraker trails that make Golden a Rockies enduro hub.
heads_up: Mostly black terrain; limited beginner options; short bike-park season

name: Kicking Horse River
why: Glacial class III-IV through the Lower Canyon beside Yoho National Park makes Golden the Canadian Rockies' rafting hub.
heads_up: Cold glacial water; Lower Canyon closes at high flows

name: Killarney (La Cloche Silhouette Trail)
why: White quartzite ridges over turquoise lakes painted by the Group of Seven; George Lake access with a permit-based interior paddling network.
heads_up: Backcountry sites book months out; black flies in June

name: Killington
why: The Beast of the East: largest resort in the eastern US, World Cup host, longest season and a big lift-served bike park.
heads_up: Access-road crowds and busy weekends

name: Kincardine / Station Beach
why: Lake Huron's established surf town, home of the Canadian Great Lakes surf community and the Surf Ontario pier break.
heads_up: Wind-driven swell; cold water; pier and jetty hazards

name: King Mountain
why: Long-running King Mountain Championships and record XC flights along the Lost River Range make it a destination big-air site.
heads_up: Huge thermals, strong wind and remote retrieval; experts only

name: Kingdom Swim (Lake Memphremagog)
why: Kingdom Games' flagship with 1-mile to 25 km Border Buster courses on Lake Memphremagog, repeatedly listed among the world's top 100 open-water swims.
heads_up: No guide buoys on the 10-miler; kayak escort required

name: Kingdom Trails / Burke Mountain
why: 100+ miles of flowing singletrack on private land plus the Burke Mountain lift-served park make it the Northeast's premier trail destination.
heads_up: Membership pass required; some landowner closures

name: Kingston (CORK)
why: The 1976 Olympic sailing venue and self-styled Freshwater Sailing Capital of the World (CORK hosts 1,000+ boats a season), with dozens of 19th-century wrecks (Wolfe Islander II, Munson, Comet) off the harbour for divers.
heads_up: Lake Ontario chop; cold water; boat charters needed for the wrecks

name: Kirkwood
why: Tahoe's expert mountain: the Cirque, the Wall and 600 inches of snowfall at the highest base in the region.
heads_up: Carson Pass road closures; remote with little lodging

name: Kite Beach, Jupiter / Juno
why: A1A marker 33 is South Florida's busiest ocean kite launch, rideable in every direction but west with warm Gulf Stream water most of the year.
heads_up: Shore pound and crowds; kiting banned at guarded beaches

name: Kitsilano Beach / English Bay
why: Vancouver's open-water community trains off Kits Beach and English Bay, home to the Polar Bear Swim since 1920 and the Bay Challenge crossing.
heads_up: Cold Pacific water; log booms and boat traffic

name: Kona (Honokohau)
why: One of the most famous dives in the world: dozens of manta rays feeding in dive lights at Garden Eel Cove, run nightly by the Kona charter fleet.
heads_up: Charter costs; seasickness on long days; grander fish are rare

name: Kootenay Rockwall Trail
why: The 55 km Rockwall between Paint Pots and Floe Lake is one of the top multi-day hikes in the Canadian Rockies.
heads_up: Backcountry reservations sell out in January

name: La Cruz de Huanacaxtle (Banderas Bay Regatta)
why: Vallarta Yacht Club's Banderas Bay Regatta (30+ years) is Mexico's premier cruiser regatta, sailed in 10-18 kn afternoon thermals with flat seas.
heads_up: Wind builds mid-afternoon; summer is hurricane season

name: La Huasteca
why: Monterrey's home crag in Parque Nacional Cumbres, with steep limestone sport and multipitch on the canyon walls.
heads_up: Urban-edge park; go with locals, summer heat

name: La Jolla Sea Caves
venueType: coastal sea caves and marine reserve
why: San Diego's signature snorkel and dive site inside an ecological reserve, with leopard sharks in summer, sea lions, kelp and the La Jolla Canyon.
heads_up: Sea lion closures, stingrays and shorebreak at the Shores

name: La Malinche
why: The standard acclimatisation hike for Orizaba and Izta, with a well-trodden trail from the IMSS resort to the summit.
heads_up: Altitude; afternoon clouds, start early

name: La Paz
why: Espiritu Santo's sea-lion colony, whale-shark snorkelling in the bay and the El Bajo seamount make La Paz the Sea of Cortez's established dive hub.
heads_up: Los Islotes closed June-August for pupping; long boat rides

name: La Push / First Beach
why: The Olympic Peninsula's established surf beach on Quileute land, known for the Hobuck/La Push surf community and consistent beach-break waves.
heads_up: Remote; respect Quileute Nation rules; cold water and logs in the water

name: La Saladita / Troncones
why: A mellow 300-metre left point that is the established longboard destination of the Zihuatanejo coast.
heads_up: Rocky entry at low tide; summer heat and mosquitoes

name: La Ventana
why: North America's winter wind capital: El Norte blows most days November to March over warm Sea of Cortez water, with dozens of schools, foil camps and the La Ventana Classic.
heads_up: Downwind drift to the point; busy launch in January

name: Lady Bird Lake, Austin
why: A motor-free downtown lake with several long-standing SUP outfitters (Austin Rowing Club, Live Love Paddle) and year-round paddling.
heads_up: Summer heat; crowded weekends; bat bridge sunset traffic

name: Laguna Bacalar
why: The 'Lagoon of Seven Colours', a motor-restricted 42 km freshwater lagoon with cenotes and stromatolites, paddled by SUP and kayak from lakeside balnearios and rental docks; Mexico's most established flatwater paddling destination.
heads_up: No sunscreen in stromatolite zones; midday heat; afternoon wind

name: Laguna Madre (Port Mansfield / Port Aransas)
why: The Lower Laguna Madre is the US's premier redfish and seatrout sight-fishing flat, with a dedicated skiff-guide culture.
heads_up: Wind; shallow prop-scar restrictions; summer heat

name: Lake Dillon
why: Dillon Yacht Club at 9,017 ft is the highest yacht club in North America and runs the Dillon Open, the world's highest regatta, in 6-25 kn mountain wind.
heads_up: Altitude, sudden squalls, very cold water

name: Lake Elsinore / Edwards Launch
why: Long-established Southern California thermal and ridge site above Lake Elsinore with multiple launches and a dedicated LZ.
heads_up: Strong lake-breeze afternoons; landing field access rules change

name: Lake Louise
why: World Cup opener venue in Banff National Park with 4,200 acres of back bowls and some of the best scenery in skiing.
heads_up: Very cold January temperatures; national park pass required

name: Lake Louise / Back of the Lake
why: The Back of the Lake quartzite crag is the Rockies' best-known cragging, while Plain of Six Glaciers and Lake Agnes are Banff's signature hikes.
heads_up: Parking reservations and shuttles; grizzly closures

name: Lake O'Hara (Yoho)
why: The Alpine Circuit and Lake Oesa trails make Lake O'Hara the Rockies' most coveted and most restricted hiking destination.
heads_up: Bus lottery only; no private vehicles

name: Lake Powell / Antelope Canyon
why: Paddling from Antelope Point into the flooded lower Antelope Canyon slot is Lake Powell's signature kayak trip with rentals at the marina.
heads_up: Summer heat; afternoon wind and boat wakes on open water

name: Lake Tahoe / Emerald Bay & Desolation Wilderness
why: Emerald Bay anchors the Lake Tahoe Water Trail and California's first underwater maritime heritage trail, and the Eagle Lake, Lake Aloha and Tahoe Rim trails above it are the most popular wilderness hiking in Northern California.
heads_up: Afternoon wind and cold 50F water; day-use permits at Eagle Falls, overnight quotas

name: Lake Tahoe / Kings Beach and Sand Harbor
why: Host of Ta-Hoe Nalu, the world's oldest SUP race (since 2007), and the Thunderbird Paddling Festival at Sand Harbor.
heads_up: Altitude (6,200 ft); cold water; afternoon wind; AIS inspection for boards

name: Lake Tahoe East Shore (Sand Harbor / Flume Trail)
why: Host of the Trans Tahoe Relay since 1976 and a hub for length-of-lake marathon swims, with the Flume Trail and bike-legal Tahoe Rim Trail sections above Sand Harbor as bucket-list rides.
heads_up: Altitude (6,200 ft); 55-62F water; TRT bike days alternate even/odd

name: Lake Union, Seattle
why: Seattle's established urban SUP venue with multiple rental centres and skyline and houseboat paddling routes.
heads_up: Seaplane and boat traffic; stay near the shoreline

name: Lakeview (Black Cap / Sugar Hill)
why: Self-styled Hang Gliding Capital of the West; hosts the Lakeview Fly-In and US Nationals with Black Cap launch above town.
heads_up: Strong, hot desert thermals and big XC terrain; retrieval distances

name: Lanai Cathedrals
why: First and Second Cathedral, sunlit lava caverns on Lanai's south shore, are Maui County's most celebrated dives and run daily from Lahaina.
heads_up: Boat crossing from Maui; overhead environment

name: Lander / Wild Iris & Sinks Canyon
why: Home of the International Climbers' Festival, with Wild Iris's pocketed dolomite and Sinks Canyon's year-round limestone.
heads_up: Wild Iris sits at 9,000 ft; snow until June

name: Larchmont / Long Island Sound
why: Larchmont Race Week (since 1896) and the dense yacht-club coastline of western Long Island Sound form the New York area's racing heartland.
heads_up: Light summer wind; heavy weekend traffic

name: Lauderdale-by-the-Sea / Fort Lauderdale
why: Broward's main ocean kite beach, with winter frontal and thermal winds and designated launch corridors at Lauderdale-by-the-Sea, Pompano and Tiki Beach.
heads_up: Stay 100 yd outside swim buoys; shore pound

name: Lawrencetown Beach
why: Atlantic Canada's surf hub, a provincial park beach with surf schools and the Lawrencetown Left Point for hurricane swells.
heads_up: Wetsuit year-round; big late-summer hurricane swell; rips

name: Le Massif de Charlevoix
why: The highest vertical east of the Rockies (2,526 ft) dropping straight toward the St. Lawrence, with a national training downhill.
heads_up: Summit-access layout; wind off the river

name: Leavenworth / Icicle Creek
why: Washington's biggest concentration of granite trad, sport and bouldering in Icicle Creek and Tumwater canyons, with the Enchantments trailheads nearby.
heads_up: Summer crowds; wildfire smoke in late summer

name: Lees Ferry
why: Fifteen miles of cold Colorado River tailwater below Glen Canyon Dam with wild rainbows and a boat-up guide culture in Marble Canyon.
heads_up: Boat access only for the upper river; fluctuating dam releases; desert heat in summer

name: Lehigh River Gorge
why: Francis E. Walter Dam release weekends through Lehigh Gorge State Park make it the Northeast's highest-volume beginner rafting destination.
heads_up: Release-weekend dependent; low and scrapy in midsummer

name: Les Escoumins
why: Parks Canada's dedicated dive base in the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park, with anemone-covered walls and the best-known cold-water diving in eastern Canada.
heads_up: Drysuit water; currents at Baie des Anemones

name: Lion's Head
why: Ontario's premier sport crag on the Bruce Peninsula, with the Bruce Trail along the clifftop.
heads_up: Top-down approach by rappel; tolerated use in a nature reserve, keep a low profile

name: Little Cottonwood Canyon
why: Salt Lake's granite trad testpieces and world-class bouldering minutes from the city, plus American Fork limestone nearby.
heads_up: Watershed rules (no dogs); winter road traffic

name: Lochsa River
why: Fifty-plus continuous class III-IV+ rapids along US 12 at peak snowmelt; Lochsa Madness draws paddlers from across the West each Memorial Day.
heads_up: Huge cold snowmelt flows; no dams, no bail-outs

name: Longs Peak / Rocky Mountain National Park
why: The Diamond on Longs is America's classic alpine big wall, Lumpy Ridge is a trad hub, and the Keyhole Route and Sky Pond are flagship Front Range hikes.
heads_up: Timed-entry permits; lightning and altitude

name: Looe Key
why: A Sanctuary Preservation Area in the Lower Keys, widely rated the best shallow reef in the Keys for both snorkelling and diving.
heads_up: No-take zone; shallow reef easily damaged by fins

name: Lookout Mountain (Golden)
why: Denver's home site with the Rocky Mountain Hang Gliding and Paragliding Association, tandems and a Windy Saddle launch above Golden.
heads_up: Notoriously switchy, rotor-prone conditions; RMHPA site guidelines mandatory

name: Lookout Mountain Flight Park
why: The largest flight park in the Southeast with full-time school, tow and mountain launch, and a long-established ridge above the Lookout Valley.
heads_up: Primarily hang gliding culture; paraglider days depend on light winds; membership and ratings required

name: Loreto
venueType: island marine park and panga fishery
why: The dorado capital of Baja and a UNESCO marine park of five islands, with a decades-old panga guide fleet, established dive shops and multi-day sea-kayak operators running since the 1980s.
heads_up: Norte winds Dec-Feb; summer heat; marine park regulations

name: Los Barriles / East Cape
why: The East Cape's original windsurf town (since the 1980s), host of the Lord of the Wind kite and windsurf competition each January, and the roosterfish-from-the-beach capital with a classic Sea of Cortez panga fleet in summer.
heads_up: Shore break on big north days; heat and hurricanes in late summer

name: Los Dinamos
why: Mexico City's home crag with roughly 250 routes on Cerro Coconetla and forested hiking along the Magdalena river.
heads_up: Altitude (2,900 m+); weekend crowds; rainy season Jun-Sep

name: Lost Coast Trail
why: The 25-mile Mattole to Black Sands Beach walk is California's most famous coastal backpack through the King Range.
heads_up: Tide-dependent sections; permit quotas; shuttle logistics

name: Louisiana Marsh
why: The best big-redfish sight fishery on the planet, with fly guides out of Venice, Hopedale and Cocodrie chasing bull reds in winter.
heads_up: Cold fronts and wind; long boat runs; mosquitoes

name: Lower Trestles
why: The WSL Finals venue and the LA 2028 Olympic surfing site, inside San Onofre State Beach.
heads_up: 20-minute walk-in from the parking lot; very competitive lineup

name: Lower Youghiogheny
venueType: class III-IV river in state park
why: Ohiopyle State Park's Lower Yough is the most-paddled class III-IV in the Mid-Atlantic, with a launch permit system and outfitters in town.
heads_up: Launch permits required and capped on summer weekends

name: Lumby (Cooper's / Freedom Flight Park)
why: Home of Freedom Flight Park and the Lumby Air Force club, with the Cooper's launch used for competitions and the Canadian Nationals.
heads_up: 10 hours airtime minimum for Cooper's; thermic Okanagan afternoons

name: Mackinac Island
why: Finish line of both the Chicago and Bayview (Port Huron) Mackinac races, making it the Great Lakes' most celebrated sailing destination each July.
heads_up: No cars; harbour packed during race week

name: Mad River Glen
why: Skier-owned co-op with the famous single chair, natural snow and the 'Ski It If You Can' legend.
heads_up: Snowboards banned; natural snow only

name: Madawaska River (Palmer Rapids)
why: The Madawaska Kanu Centre has taught whitewater here since 1972; the warm class II-III Lower Mad is Canada's paddling school river.
heads_up: Low water by late summer; school-based access

name: Madison River
why: The '50-mile riffle' between Quake Lake and Ennis is one of the most-floated trout rivers in the world with a dense fly-shop and guide culture.
heads_up: Salmonfly crowds in late June; wade-only and float-only sections; wind

name: Magdalen Islands (Havre-aux-Basques)
why: A Gulf of St. Lawrence archipelago of shallow, shark-free lagoons with wind nearly every day; Aerosport has taught here since 1998 and it is eastern Canada's windsport destination.
heads_up: Ferry or flight access; autumn storms

name: Magdalena Bay
